key_insight: A semi-supervised machine learning model trained on rectal biopsy RNA-seq can help predict which ulcerative colitis patients are likely to relapse after stopping anti-TNF therapy.
clinical_relevance: This could support safer treatment withdrawal decisions by identifying high-risk patients before anti-TNF discontinuation, while avoiding relapse in those more likely to remain in remission.
method: Prospective BIOSTOP trial cohort of 136 ulcerative colitis patients.
Built a semi-supervised model using baseline rectal biopsy transcriptomics and a shared UMAP + LabelSpreading approach.
Focused on a targeted 38-gene panel and interpreted predictions with SHAP.
evidence_signal: The model reached AUC 0.794, 90.3% sensitivity, and 73.1% specificity in the test cohort, with AUC 0.711 in the inference cohort.
watch_item: Specificity was only moderate, so the model needs multi-center validation in larger and more diverse cohorts before clinical use.
paper_title: Machine learning predicts relapse after anti-TNF withdrawal in ulcerative colitis using rectal biopsy transcriptomics
